design_principles_established: Three-tier output: (a) skill templates = drop-in code, (b) report scaffolds = starter code with TODOs, (c) advisories = developer-decision-only items in Developer Recommendations Report.
Developer Recommendations Report = extension of existing /llm-secure-patterns:report command. Includes scaffolded code where possible.
Main posture report framed as CTO report: strategic posture, what was applied and where.
Report entries must be self-contained — spell out domain terms (e.g., 'Stage 1 (classification/reasoning stage)').
Warnings about what a skill does NOT cover live in SKILL.md. Developer Recommendations Report only echoes them when the skill actually fired. CTO report never lists adjacent gaps.

Plan-scan mode deferred to v1.1 (CHANGELOG): /llm-secure-patterns:plan-scan reads a project plan, batches all tier/architecture decisions upfront, writes .llm-security-decisions.yaml so skills can run mostly unattended.

decisions.title: Separate inference pool — Claude API viability
decisions.original_note: need more info on what separate inference pools are.
decisions.resolution: Drop the 'pool' jargon entirely. Reframe Level C as: 'Separate credentials per trust tier. Use a distinct API key, system prompt, and rate limit for each trust tier. The Claude API does not offer a named inference pool primitive — key-level separation is the practical equivalent on today's APIs.'

targets.cto_report: posture entry: trust-tier credential isolation applied
targets.dev_report: scaffold: two Anthropic() clients with distinct keys labeled low_trust_client / high_trust_client, with .env example and usage guidance

decisions.title: Token estimation heuristic — ship or require real tokenizer
decisions.original_note: why do we not put a length code. or could we ask them to choose during development? And still add warning?
decisions.resolution: Keep len/4 heuristic but use Anthropic SDK's client.messages.count_tokens() (NOT tiktoken — wrong tokenizer for Claude) as the accurate path. Side-by-side code blocks with prominent # WARNING: NOT PRODUCTION-SAFE above the heuristic. Interactive choice deferred to v1.1 plan-scan.

targets.cto_report: posture entry noting heuristic used with accuracy caveat (underestimates CJK/emoji 2-4x)
targets.dev_report: action item: switch to client.messages.count_tokens() before serving non-English traffic or relying on token counts for billing/quota

decisions.title: Input size check — elevate warning or remove
decisions.resolution: Promote parenthetical CJK/emoji warning to # WARNING inline comment above the len(request.message) > MAX_INPUT_CHARS check. Match Level B style. No behavior change.

decisions.title: Output-validation trigger scope vs. HTML-only implementation
decisions.original_note: can we give a warning that it does not do string escaping for SQL/shell commands? as well as your suggested resolution.
decisions.resolution: Narrow SKILL.md trigger to HTML/markup rendering contexts only. Add explicit warning: 'This skill does NOT provide SQL or shell escaping. For SQL use parameterized queries (cursor.execute(sql, params) — never string interpolation). For shell use argument arrays (subprocess.run([cmd, arg]) — never shell=True with user input).'

targets.dev_report: one-line reminder when Output Validation was applied: 'This skill covered HTML escaping only. SQL and shell contexts require parameterized queries and argument arrays respectively.'

decisions.title: sanitize_html_output name implies context-agnostic safety
decisions.resolution: Rename sanitize_html_output() to escape_html_text_node() in template + all call sites + SKILL.md references. Docstring: 'Safe for text-node insertion only. Not safe for attribute, JS, CSS, or URL contexts.'

decisions.title: Fail-closed logic uses string-matching on warning messages
decisions.resolution: Refactor scan functions to return structured dicts {type, severity, match}. Fail-closed block matches on 'type' field instead of message substring. Breaking template API change — acceptable pre-release.

decisions.title: Dual-prompt architecture — no implementation path
decisions.original_note: suggested sounds good. should we have an additional developer recommendations report we provide with recommendations to developer for items we cannot solve?
decisions.resolution: Reframe Level C: 'No API placement makes a system prompt inaccessible to the model. Dual-prompt refers to separating user-visible instructions from internal reasoning — not cryptographic confidentiality.' Provide concrete example: system parameter vs. assistant prefill. Originating prompt for the Developer Recommendations Report idea (now locked in as Option B with code scaffolds).

targets.dev_report: scaffold: system-parameter vs. assistant-prefill split in working code, explaining what dual-prompt does/doesn't give you

decisions.title: Output filter for Level C — no template or adversarial guidance
decisions.original_note: suggested is good. make sure this goes into developer recommendations report also.
decisions.resolution: Demote full template to v1.0.1. In v1.0.0 add cross-reference + keyword-blocklist starter: 'A filter prompt template with adversarial evasion caveats will be added in v1.0.1. For now, implement a keyword blocklist for known system prompt fragments as a starting point.'

targets.changelog: v1.0.1 roadmap entry for filter template
targets.dev_report: entry: 'Level C output filter template planned for v1.0.1. Interim mitigation: keyword blocklist matching known system prompt fragments. The filter itself is an LLM call and is susceptible to the same adversarial techniques it's designed to catch — plan for false negatives.'

decisions.title: Credential regex patterns — illustrative vs. maintained
decisions.original_note: Yes. any reason we don't already suggest implementation of trufflehog as part of this skill? or is that not done, or otherwise risky?
decisions.resolution: Keep illustrative regex with prominent caveat. Add new section in SKILL.md: 'Recommended tooling — for real-time output scanning use detect-secrets (Python library); for repo/git-history scanning use truffleHog (CLI). These maintain up-to-date detector sets and are the production-grade path. The regex in this template is illustrative only.' Distinction: this skill's use case is runtime output scanning (detect-secrets fits); truffleHog matters for preventing accidentally committed secrets.

targets.cto_report: posture entry: illustrative credential regex in use; production detection delegated to maintained scanners
targets.dev_report: install + integration snippets: pip install detect-secrets (3-line runtime scan example); trufflehog filesystem --directory=. (pre-commit hook pointer)

decisions.title: Cross-tag escape — only escapes current iteration's tag
decisions.resolution: build_system_prompt() collects ALL registered tag names, then applies a single combined regex to every content block. Closes the 'close one UNTRUSTED block, open a different registered tag' bypass.

decisions.title: CLEAN output label creates false confidence
decisions.resolution: Change demo output from 'Credential scan: CLEAN' to 'No credential patterns detected'. Scopes what was scanned ('credential') and implies 'we looked, didn't find' rather than a binary pass. Drop the parenthetical — 'detected' carries the caveat.

targets.template: all templates with demo print statements (credential scans, PII scans)

decisions.title: Destructive tool denylist — expand or flip to allowlist
decisions.original_note: agreed. should we add note to developer in recommendations report?
decisions.resolution: Flip DESTRUCTIVE_TOOL_PREFIXES denylist to SAFE_READ_PREFIXES allowlist: {'get', 'list', 'read', 'fetch', 'search', 'describe'}. Anything not on the list flagged as potentially destructive. Promote caveat from docstring to # WARNING block at call site.

targets.dev_report: entry: 'Agent Action Surface uses a read-only allowlist (SAFE_READ_PREFIXES). Any tool not matching the allowlist is flagged as potentially destructive. Review and extend the allowlist for your specific MCP servers and tool sets — safe tool names vary by provider.'

decisions.title: Stage 1 write-permission enforcement language
decisions.original_note: agreed. maybe developer recommendations report also
decisions.resolution: SKILL.md language change: 'Stage 1 should not have write permissions. validate_pipeline() will warn if it detects them but cannot enforce this at runtime.' Add validate_or_raise() variant for hard-fail callers.

targets.dev_report: entry: 'validate_pipeline() warns on Stage 1 (classification/reasoning stage) write permissions but cannot prevent them at runtime. Use validate_or_raise() to fail hard on detection, or enforce at the deployment layer (IAM roles, API key scoping, least-privilege service accounts) to block Stage 1 from ever acquiring write capability. Preventing write-capable Stage 1 pipelines is the operator's responsibility.'

decisions.title: MCP tool schema injection — in scope or out
decisions.original_note: Agreed. but is this actionable by developer, or just protecting our credibility? Anything else we can help them with?
decisions.resolution: Replace one-line caveat with 'MCP server trust' subsection in Level B covering 6 controls: (1) allowlist MCP servers, (2) pin schema hashes + diff on change, (3) sanitize tool descriptions (apply delimiter-escape), (4) bound-check schema structure at registration, (5) registration audit log, (6) least-privilege at MCP boundary. Lead framing: 'MCP tool schemas influence model behavior before any code runs. Hash-pinning surfaces schema changes that would otherwise slip past normal code review because they don't break your code.' Verify Palo Alto Unit 42 citation before shipping; drop reference if no specific paper is locatable. Include false-confidence warning: controls mitigate common MCP trust failures, do not eliminate risk from deeply compromised server with valid credentials.

targets.skill_md: skills/agent-action-surface/SKILL.md (new MCP server trust subsection in Level B)
targets.cto_report: posture entry: 'MCP schema-trust controls applied: allowlist + hash-pinning + description escaping. Rug-pull attacks mitigated at registration time.' Includes false-confidence warning.
targets.dev_report: scaffolds: allowlist config + hash-pinning helper (with pin-update workflow — on mismatch, show diff and require confirmation like SSH known_hosts). Include MCP spec version note.

decisions.title: Audit logging 'full context' creates LLM02 surface
decisions.original_note: hmm. are changes you suggest going to impact skill, or just suggestions to dev?
decisions.resolution: Three layers: (1) SKILL.md swap 'full context' → 'relevant context' + add framing: 'Logging full context creates an LLM02 sensitive-information-disclosure surface. Logs become a new attack target; anyone who compromises log storage inherits your system prompts, user PII, and credentials from tool results.' (2) Template code: add redact_for_audit_log() helper — drops system prompt contents (log hash only), masks known credential patterns (integrates with detect-secrets from #9), drops/masks PII fields flagged by caller, logs tool name + parameter schema not parameter values (opt-in per-field). (3) Dev report: deployment checklist (access controls on log storage, retention limits, storage encryption at rest, log destination trust review, separation of audit from operational logs).

targets.cto_report: posture entry: audit logging applied with redaction helper; deployment-layer controls flagged as operator responsibility
targets.dev_report: deployment checklist with rationale per item, no code

decisions.title: trusts_input_from=None default silently suppresses warnings
decisions.resolution: Remove '= None' default from trusts_input_from parameter. Omission now raises a validation error at pipeline construction time. Breaking change — acceptable pre-release.
